findings.title: RoBERTa-large SQuAD 2.0 preserves task metrics in fp16 on CPU, while fp16 is slower than fp32 on this host
findings.observation: At winml 0.2.0 on current-main 904c20109ab31d737c5132c3686ab404236edd57, deepset/roberta-large-squad2 built from the nested CPU recipes at fp32 and fp16. CPUExecutionProvider perf (20 measured, 5 warmup) was fp32 mean/p50 902.339/904.426 ms, 1.11 samples/s, RSS model-load delta 1167.0 MB; fp16 mean/p50 1041.909/1040.757 ms, 0.96 samples/s, RSS model-load delta 1180.8 MB. Both artifacts scored exact 85.0 and F1 88.70079365079366 on rajpurkar/squad_v2 validation, 100 shuffled samples, seed 42. CLI compare against the HF reference gave fp32 mean cosine 0.9999999999794873/0.9999999999866034 and fp16 0.9999928808311433/0.9999945743800909 for start/end logits. The optimized fp32 graph has 865 operators, 20 op types; top counts are Add 244, MatMul 193, Mul 97 (then Reshape 96 and Transpose 96). Full --ep all analysis found QNN GPU partial Div, Erf, Add, Mul and no unsupported op types; NVIDIA TensorRT RTX and OpenVINO GPU classified all 20 op types supported; CUDA, MIGraphX, and DML had all 20 unknown because no rule rows exist. export_htp_metadata reports 354,312,194 parameters, 443 modules, 172 traced modules, rooted at RobertaForQuestionAnswering -> RobertaModel -> embeddings + 24-layer encoder, plus qa_outputs. The input recipe optim block remained clamp_constant_values=true; autoconf did not add another optimization pass.
gotchas: For fp16, use --precision fp16 without --no-quant; verify 396 FLOAT16 initializers and model.onnx.data near 709.7 MB instead of the fp32 1,419.3 MB.
CPU fp16 preserved exact/F1 on this subset but was slower than fp32; report measured values rather than assuming reduced precision is faster.
findings.mechanism_notes: Exact task metrics were equal on the tested deterministic subset and the artifact dtype/size difference was inspected directly. Performance scope is this host only.

findings.title: The RoBERTa QA fp16 recipe must own quant intent to realize fp16 weights while preserving float logits
findings.observation: At microsoft/winml-cli candidate fdf697a741909c34932354f4af2560eea6efbc71 with winml-cli 0.2.0 and onnxruntime-windowsml 1.24.5.202604171637, the CPU fp16 recipe for deepset/roberta-large-squad2 carried quant.mode=fp16, task/model identity, and fp16_keep_io_types=true. A fresh recipe build produced 394 FLOAT16 initializers, no FLOAT initializers, FLOAT start/end logits, and 708,632,592 external-data bytes versus 394 FLOAT initializers and 1,417,256,976 bytes for fp32 (ratio 0.5000029). On one pinned SQuAD v2 validation row, fp16 start/end cosine versus PyTorch was 0.9999999707/0.9999999429 with max-abs 0.0115833/0.0143809 and the same decoded span, France. CPU perf over 20 measured iterations plus 5 warmups was fp32 mean/p50 629.132/625.715 ms at 1.59 samples/s and fp16 750.687/746.023 ms at 1.33 samples/s, so realized fp16 remained slower on this host. The required final-SHA L3 check was deliberately bounded to two deterministic fp32 SQuAD v2 validation rows, two tokenized features, and two model inferences; exact match and F1 were both 100, proving functional smoke operability only, not benchmark accuracy or fp16 task accuracy.
evidence: Tester verdict SHA-256 3c787830d86231097c5fe3a8251c5023e65c187594306a4cedfe699105c2b593; sealed raw-evidence manifest SHA-256 af81365b288f0fb8d6d7136e506c34daa97eb2105cf022d02cefa052127889d4.

findings.title: RoBERTa-large QA maps completely to embeddings, 24 encoder layers, and the QA head, with QNN indexing ops requiring attention
findings.observation: For the fp32 and fp16 artifacts built from microsoft/winml-cli candidate fdf697a741909c34932354f4af2560eea6efbc71, HTP metadata reports 354,312,194 parameters, 443 modules, and 172 traced modules. The traced top-level hierarchy is RobertaForQuestionAnswering -> RobertaModel -> RobertaEmbeddings plus RobertaEncoder with 24 RobertaLayer children -> qa_outputs; layer children include self-attention and attention output, intermediate GELU, and feed-forward output. Source-derived component mapping covered all 749 fp32 and 751 fp16 ONNX nodes: embeddings 17; self-attention 391; intermediate/GELU 72; feed-forward output 144; attention-output/residual/layer orchestration 120; QA head 5 fp32 or 7 fp16. Direct module scopes covered 497 nodes in each graph; 252 fp32 and 254 fp16 optimizer-generated nodes were assigned by execution adjacency, with zero unmapped. The manifest-backed analyze outputs contain 21 operator types: both graphs are dominated by Reshape 243, Gemm 145, Transpose 96, Add 75, LayerNormalization 49, and MatMul 48; fp16 differs by two extra Cast nodes. QNN rule data classifies Gather and GatherElements partial, affecting embedding/indexing and one attention-region Gather; Where is unknown for NvTensorRTRTX, QNN, and OpenVINO. CUDA, MIGraphX, TensorRT, and DML returned no shipped rule classifications. The analyze command exited 1 because --ep all includes unavailable or unclassified providers, but emitted complete structured results for all seven requested EPs and is therefore partial success, not a failed or missing analysis.
evidence: Pinned model-breakdown SHA-256 7757283795a3339f4d66b8bcf12652f8f384baeca82ed8ea540b482858fd3f9e establishes embeddings, encoder/layers, self-attention, intermediate/output, and QA-head source hierarchy.

Manifest-backed raw analyze outputs: fp32 9bc88789719bfdc229fe3581a57b6b02ee24dd5e667863af98e4ff5f4e1e1206; fp16 440f7183f7891bfa4ccdc06150aa27b32860673d2ccfc4a4d95cbb6f2a3949ec. Component mappings: fp32 30f4dc82a69b1242f73ceea9a85605a16473c58f4f5379c453677969395f52aa; fp16 f33775c19f8fb8f58dc176a6611723f5fd1a053a0165fa37155c12fe42bb0597.
